q.line: O it's not a desert nor a web
stanza: O it's not a desert nor a web
Nor a tomb where I lay dead
Minor in a sound alone
Yes a clear commanding tone

partner.line: Nor a tomb where I lay dead

q.line: We must talk in every telephone, get eaten off the web
stanza: We must talk in every telephone, get eaten off the web
We must rip out all the epilogues from the books that we have read
Into the face of every criminal strapped firmly to a chair
We must stare, we must stare, we must stare

partner.line: We must rip out all the epilogues from the books that we have read

stanza: There's a city, draped in net
Fisherman net
And in the half light, in the half light
It looks like every tower
Is covered in webs
Moving and glistening and rocking
Its babies in rhythm
As the spider of time is climbing
Over the ruins

q.line: And he's charming as a cherub as he leads you to his web
stanza: Romeo is reeling, counting notches on his thighbone
Searching for one hundred and eleven
And he's charming as a cherub as he leads you to his web
Seducing queens and gypsy girls in the boudoir of his head
Then he wraps himself with a tablecloth and pretends he is a bed
And my shoulders had to shrug as I crawled beneath the rug
And retuned my piano

partner.line: Searching for one hundred and eleven
